title: Learning: Seen in Public
text: A new base image arrives, signed. The registry can look for that signature in the public log, and the deployer can ask what is inside the image.
held: The signature was made in the open, and the contents were known before rollout.

cards.label: Reject the image
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: transparency log
fields.value: entry present, made at build time
fields.check: Look the signature up in the transparency log
fields.ok: Logged when it was signed. Anyone can see that it was.

intrusion.detail: Signed, but never logged. Nobody could have noticed this signature being made.
intrusion.why: A valid signature that isn't in the public log may have been made in secret with a stolen key. The log is how a theft gets noticed.
intrusion.reveal: The base image's signature was valid but had never been recorded in the transparency log.

cards.label: Hold the rollout
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: known flaws
fields.check: Check the image's contents list against known flaws
fields.ok: Scan of the SBOM is clean: nothing above low.

intrusion.value: critical: remote code execution in an image library
intrusion.detail: The contents list includes a library with a critical, exploitable flaw.
intrusion.why: The image was authentic and still dangerous. Knowing what is inside is a separate question from knowing who built it.
intrusion.reveal: The base image contained a library with a critical known flaw.

temptations.label: Turn the admission policy off for this one rollout
temptations.why: A policy that is switched off when it is inconvenient protects nothing. The exception becomes the route in.

teaches: A signature proves who signed. The transparency log proves it was done in the open.
Authentic is not the same as safe: a correctly built image can still contain a known flaw.
An SBOM lets you answer “are we affected?” in minutes.
